title: We Plough the Fields and Scatter
alsoKnownAs: We Plow the Fields and Scatter
description: We Plough the Fields and Scatter in Tonic Solfa to WIR PFLÜGEN: the solfa with the words, staff notation, the 3 verses and the refrain, and a piano.
about: Matthias Claudius wrote the German poem in 1782, and Jane Montgomery Campbell’s English translation dates from 1861. The tune WIR PFLÜGEN is by Johann Abraham Peter Schulz, from 1800.
underlay: We plough the fields, and scat-ter The good seed on the land, But it is fed and wa_-ter’d By God’s Al-might-y Hand; He sends the snow in win-ter, The warmth to swell the grain, The breez-es, and the sun-shine, And soft re-fresh-ing rain. All good gifts a-round us Are sent from Heav’n a-bove, Then thank the Lord, O thank the Lord, For all__ His love.

lines: We plough the fields, and scatter
The good seed on the land,
But it is fed and water’d
He sends the snow in winter,
The warmth to swell the grain,

verses.label: Refrain
lines: Then thank the Lord, O thank the Lord,
Of all things near and far;
The winds and waves obey Him,
By Him the birds are fed;
Much more to us, His children,
We thank Thee then, O Father,
For all things bright and good,
Our life, our health, our food;
